title: King Saul teaches one of the most painful leadership lessons in the Bible.
paragraphs: King Saul teaches one of the most painful leadership lessons in the Bible.
God chose him.
Out of all the tribes of Israel, God placed Saul on the throne.

He was tall. Strong. Impressive.
The kind of man people expected a king to be.
But beneath the crown was a heart struggling with insecurity.
The moment that revealed it came after a victory.
Women began singing in the streets:

“Saul has slain his thousands,
and David his ten thousands.”
It was just a song.
But insecurity hears comparison even when celebration is happening.
From that moment forward, Saul did not see David as a blessing.
He saw him as a threat.
And insecurity does something dangerous:
It turns allies into enemies.

David was loyal.
David fought for Saul’s kingdom.
David played the harp to calm Saul’s troubled spirit.
Yet Saul tried to kill him.

Not once.
Multiple times.
Here is the tragedy of insecurity:
Saul feared losing a throne that God had already given him.

When you don’t trust the God who placed you somewhere,
you will constantly fear someone taking your place.
And insecurity rarely destroys you overnight.
It slowly reshapes your decisions.

It makes you compete where you should celebrate.
Attack where you should mentor.
Control where you should trust.
One of the most haunting lines in Saul’s story is this:
“So Saul eyed David from that day forward.”
A king chosen by God became a man controlled by comparison.
And eventually, insecurity cost him everything.
Here is the lesson:

If you don’t deal with insecurity in your heart,
you may start fighting the very people God sent to help your calling.
Some destinies are not destroyed by enemies.
They are destroyed by comparison.
And Saul is the warning.
